targeting_context.jd_text:
Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships
San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic's products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities

    Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
    Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic's GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
    Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
    Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
    Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
    Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic's products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have

    7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
    3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
    Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
    Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
    Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
    Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
    A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have

    5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
    Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Compensation

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role's On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000-$380,000 OTE | Reports to Partnerships (partner-facing GTM) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s central ecosystem challenge is converting frontier-model capability into dependable enterprise value through third parties without diluting technical quality, customer trust, or safety expectations.

The tension is scale versus consistency. Partners extend industry knowledge, implementation capacity, and commercial reach, while Anthropic needs clear standards for architecture, governance, escalation, and customer outcomes.

This role sits where technical credibility, partner economics, field learning, and responsible deployment meet. Success is likely measured by whether an expanding ecosystem can produce repeatable customer results rather than isolated
technical wins.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is an AI safety and research company focused on reliable, interpretable, and steerable systems. Its public-benefit-corporation structure reinforces that safety is not separate from product and commercial decisions.

Claude serves both business users and technical builders. That creates a broad adoption surface: organizations may begin with knowledge-work use cases, developer workflows, or integrated applications, then expand across functions.

The company’s enterprise strategy combines a product platform with external distribution and delivery capacity. Cloud, services, and technology firms can help customers operationalize Claude, but Anthropic remains accountable for a
coherent experience and a high bar for production use.

For a partnerships architecture leader, the practical mandate is to create an operating model in which external delivery capacity grows faster than central technical involvement without losing quality control.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic operates in a market where model capability alone does not determine enterprise adoption. Buyers also evaluate security, governance, integration effort, provider credibility, implementation support, and the ability to
demonstrate sustained business value.

Its portfolio spans enterprise workplace usage, coding-oriented experiences, and API-based product integration. These paths require distinct technical patterns, yet customers will expect a unified point of view on identity,
administration, evaluation, risk management, and organizational adoption.

Enterprise guidance signals that rollout is a multi-stage change program, not merely a software activation. Technical configuration, user readiness, training, and ongoing expansion all affect whether an initial deployment becomes
durable usage.

The likely operating pressure is balancing fast-moving field demand with centralized standards from product, engineering, security, and policy stakeholders. Strong decision rights will matter: which patterns are reusable, which cases
require deeper review, and which field signals warrant product investment.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
The role requires influence across a company that brings together research, engineering, policy, product, and commercial functions. Partner activity will often create questions that cannot be resolved by a single organization.

Key internal interfaces are likely to include:
- Safety, security, and policy colleagues responsible for preserving trustworthy deployment practices as usage scales.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Claude is positioned for complex reasoning, data analysis, coding, and knowledge-work support. That flexibility creates opportunity, but it also raises the need for disciplined solution design and clear customer qualification.

API availability makes integration design a major component of value realization. Partners will need practical patterns for application workflows, evaluation methods, human oversight, operational monitoring, and iterative improvement.

Enterprise administration guidance indicates that successful deployments involve more than model access. Identity, access controls, configuration, onboarding, training, usage measurement, and organizational sponsorship all shape
adoption.

The important architecture opportunity is not generic prompt advice. It is developing reusable ways to connect AI capabilities to real operating workflows while making reliability, security, user experience, and governance visible
to customers.

Anthropic’s emphasis on steerability and reliability should inform the partner narrative. The strongest partner solutions will frame controlled, measurable deployment as a source of enterprise confidence and commercial differentiation.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly presents an ecosystem spanning cloud, technology, and services providers. These categories are complementary rather than independent: cloud firms contribute distribution and infrastructure context; service
providers bring delivery capacity and industry expertise; technology partners extend workflows and application reach.

A scalable ecosystem needs more than training. It needs repeatable technical assets, partner segmentation, opportunity qualification, joint account rules, escalation paths, and feedback loops that turn delivery learning into better
products and playbooks.

The highest-value work will likely be concentrated in strategic accounts and novel implementation patterns. The operating challenge is knowing where Anthropic specialists must engage directly and where qualified partners can lead
with established approaches.

A mature program should separate partner readiness from partner autonomy. Certification, enablement, and reference materials increase coverage, while governance and shared technical standards protect customers and Anthropic’s
reputation.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s enterprise materials and visible partner ecosystem indicate that the market is moving beyond experimentation toward operational adoption. The near-term priority is likely to be durable value after launch, not merely
successful demonstrations or initial access.

The growing range of customer entry points increases coordination requirements. A company may encounter Claude through a workplace deployment, developer tooling, cloud ecosystem relationship, or embedded application. The technical and
commercial story must remain connected across those paths.

In frontier AI, partner execution can materially influence adoption speed. Strong delivery organizations, trusted cloud relationships, reusable proof points, and sound production practices can accelerate expansion while reducing
implementation risk.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Establishing repeatable technical operating models for partner-led enterprise growth.
- Converting AI platform capabilities into reusable, governed solution patterns.
- Combining architecture depth with executive communication and practitioner education.
- Building disciplined loops between deployment evidence and product prioritization.
- Treating security, governance, adoption, and measurable outcomes as integrated design concerns.
- Scaling ecosystem coverage while preserving technical quality and customer confidence.
- Leading teams through ambiguity across commercial, product, engineering, and safety requirements.
- Connecting developer-led and business-led adoption into a unified enterprise strategy.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Enterprise adoption appears to depend on organizational change and user readiness alongside technology configuration.
- The combination of enterprise products and API use cases creates demand for portable architecture and governance patterns.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims must come from the governed resume/proof graph.
